transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because since my father-in-law moved in with us, I’ve been more wound up at home. I’m holding it together at work, but I’ve been short with people and it’s been harder to focus on my coursework. I’ve also stopped doing things like fishing, woodworking, and the first-aid workshops that usually help me clear my head.
How long ago did your father-in-law move in with you, and about when did you start noticing these changes in your mood and behavior?
He moved in about four months ago. I’d say within the first month or two, once we were settling into the new routines and the caregiving stuff, I started feeling the strain.
When you describe feeling 'wound up,' would you say you're mostly feeling anxious and on edge, mostly feeling sad or down, or a combination of both?
I'm not really sure how to separate those. I just know I've been more tense and irritable than usual.
Over the past couple of months, have there been at least two weeks in a row where you felt down, sad, or had little interest or pleasure in almost everything, nearly every day?
I don’t think so. I’ve been stressed and irritable, but I wouldn’t say I’ve felt down or lost interest in everything nearly every day for that long.
Aside from the situation with your father-in-law, do you find yourself worrying excessively about several different things in your life, and having a hard time controlling that worry?
I’m not sure I’d call it worrying about a lot of different things. It’s mostly been tied to what’s going on at home.

Besides feeling tense and irritable, have you noticed yourself acting out in ways that are out of character for you—like being aggressive, breaking rules, or engaging in reckless behavior since your father-in-law moved in?
No, I haven’t noticed anything like that. I’ve been more short-tempered, but I haven’t been aggressive or done anything reckless or out of character.
When you feel 'wound up,' do you also notice physical signs like a racing heart, muscle tension, restlessness, or feeling on edge, as separate from just feeling irritable?
I haven’t really noticed those kinds of physical symptoms. It’s more that I get irritated and feel wound up mentally.
Aside from feeling irritable, would you describe your emotional state as feeling nervous or anxious much of the time?
I wouldn’t say nervous or anxious all the time. I’m mostly more wound up and short at home than I usually am, since my father-in-law moved in.
